package.title: Tirzepatide (Zepbound) Single-Dose Pen Disposal: What the Pen Guide Says

social.facebook_caption:
Finished your Zepbound single-dose pen and not sure where it goes?

The pen guide is clear: right after use, it goes into an FDA-cleared sharps container. No FDA-cleared container handy? The pen guide says a household container can be used if it is all of these: heavy-duty plastic, a tight-fitting, puncture-resistant lid, upright and stable during use, leak-resistant, and properly labelled to warn of hazardous waste inside. Don't throw used pens in your household trash, and don't recycle your used sharps container. When it's almost full, follow your community guidelines.

Outside the US? UK, Canada and Australia rules differ; ask your pharmacy or local council or municipality.

Save this for your next pen day.

#Tirzepatide

Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
I'm holding this because the only source has no verified date. S1's year field is a "HOLD FOR HUMAN, DO NOT PUBLISH" note, not a date. I couldn't fix it myself because the pen guide's "Revised" line wouldn't load. The PDF at pi.lilly.com/us/zepbound-pen-us-ifu.pdf does download (300 KB, from Lilly's own guide address), but the text inside couldn't be extracted. The FDA label PDF wouldn't open either, and DailyMed and uspl.lilly.com don't include the pen guide's text. Drugs.com refused the request. A person needs to open the PDF and copy the printed "Revised MM/YYYY" line from its last page. Don't use the prescribing information date of 8/2026.

The disposal wording I could check matches the pen guide: search snippets taken from that guide, plus the standard Lilly guide wording. That covers the FDA-cleared sharps container right after use, the 5 rules for a household container (heavy-duty plastic; tight-fitting, puncture-resistant lid; upright and stable; leak-resistant; labelled as hazardous waste), community guidelines when the container is almost full, possible state or local laws, fda.gov/safesharpsdisposal (the page loads), and not recycling the container.

Separately from the hold, slide 4 needs one wording fix. It says "Don't throw used pens in your household trash", but the guide's line is about *loose* pens. Some US areas do allow a sealed sharps container in household trash under local rules, so the slide currently says more than the source does. Everything else is in scope and safe: the device note on slide 6 (KwikPens and vials have their own leaflets), the pointer for the UK, Canada and Australia, and the closing disclaimer. Once a person adds the real date and the slide 4 fix is in, this can go back through as a PASS.

issues.claim: HOLD FOR HUMAN, DO NOT PUBLISH: I couldn't read the pen guide's printed 'Revised MM/YYYY' line…
issues.problem: This is a note to staff, not a date. If it ships, viewers see it as source text, and the rules require every source to carry its real revised date. I couldn't get the date either: the PDF downloads, but its text can't be extracted, and the FDA label PDF, DailyMed and uspl.lilly.com don't have the pen guide's text.
issues.fix: A person opens https://pi.lilly.com/us/zepbound-pen-us-ifu.pdf, copies the printed 'Revised: MM/YYYY' line from the last page, and replaces the year field with exactly that (for example "Revised MM/YYYY"). Don't use the 8/2026 prescribing information date.

issues.claim: Don't throw used pens in your household trash, and don't recycle your used sharps container.
issues.problem: The pen guide's line is about loose pens ('Do not throw away (dispose of) loose pens in your household trash'). Leaving out 'loose' turns it into a ban on household trash in every case. Some US communities do allow a sealed sharps container in household trash, and the guide points people to community guidelines for that.
issues.fix: Body: "Don't throw loose used pens in your household trash, and don't recycle your used sharps container. When it's almost full, follow your community guidelines. Source: Zepbound single-dose pen Instructions for Use." Headline: "Myth: a loose used pen can go in the bin".

issues.claim: May be state or local laws
issues.problem: This is a sentence fragment, and as a card shown on its own it doesn't make sense.
issues.fix: Change the detail to "There may be state or local laws".
